אֵלָא (terebinth, i. q. אֵלָה) Ela, pr. n.
אֶלְגָּבִישׁ m. i. q. גָּבִישׁ ice, κρύσταλ-
λος, whence אַבְנֵי אֶלְגָּבִישׁ pr. stones of
ice, i. e. hail-stones, hail, Ez. 13, 11. 13.
38, 22. The word perhaps is rather
Arabic than Hebrew, viz. أَلْجِبْس, which
the Camoos p. 742 explains by الجامد
i. e. concretum, spec. congelatum. See
in אֵל II.
אַלְגּוּמִּים see אַלְמֻגִּים.
אֶלְדָּד (whom God loveth, Theophilus)
Eldad, pr. n. m. Num. 11, 26. 27.
אֶלְדָּעָה (whom God calls, see דָּעָה)
Eldaah, pr. n. of a son of Midian, Gen.
* אָלַהּ a root not in use, Arab. أَلَهَ
to worship God, to adore; mid. Kesra
to be astonished, affrighted. See note
under אֵל I; comp. אֱלוֹהַּ.
* אָלָה I. pr. to be round, rotund;
hence to be thick, fat, gross; kindr. with
r. אוּל, comp. espec. אוּל abdomen, belly,
Ps. 73, 4. Arab. أَلِيَ to have thick but-
tocks, of a man ; to have a fat tail, of a
sheep.—Hence אַלְיָה .
II. Denom. from אֵל I, where see note ;
pr. to call on God, to invoke God ; hence
1. to swear, Arab. أَلَّ for أَلَوَ Conj. IV,
V, pr. to call on God as a witness, to af-
firm by God. 1 K. 8, 31.
2. to curse, Judg. 17, 2. Hos. 4, 2.
3. to lament, to wail, pr. to call on God
for mercy, like Engl. ‘ God have mercy !’
Joel 1, 8.
Note. It may perhaps be worth in-
quiry, whether this root be not strictly
onomatopoetic, like יְלֵל, אֶלֵל ; and then
the signification which we have here put
last (no. 3), would be the primary one.
Hiph. to cause to swear, to bind by an
oath, c. acc. 1 K. 8, 31. 2 Chr. 6, 22.
1 Sam. 14, 24.—Fut. apoc. וַיֹּאֶל from
יֹאלֶה for וַיַּאֲלֶה 1 Sam. l. c.
Deriv. אָלָה and תַּאֲלָה.
אָלָה f. Kamets impure, from אָלָה no.
II, for אָאלָה, which again is for אַלְאָה,
אַלְוָה, Arab. أَلْوَة, see Lehrg. p. 509.
1. an oath. בּוֹא בְּאָלָה to come into or
under an oath, i. e. to take an oath, Neh.
10, 30 ; hence הֵבִיא בְּאָלָה to put to an
oath Ez. 17, 13. So אָלָתִי my oath, i. e.
sworn to me, Gen. 24, 41.
2. an oath of covenant, a sworn cove-
nant, Gen. 26, 28. Deut. 29, 11. 14. Ez.
3. an imprecation, curse, execration,
Num. 5, 21. Is. 24, 6. שְׁבֻעַת־אָלָה an oath
of cursing, i. e. joined with curses, Num.
5, 21. הָיָה לְאָלָה to be for an execration
Jer. 44, 12. 42, 18. Plur. אָלוֹת curses,
execrations, Num. 5, 23. Deut. 29, 11.
אַלָּה f. an oak, Josh. 24, 26, i. q. אַלּוֹן.
R. אָלַל III.
אֵלָה f. (r. אוּל) i. q. אֵיל no. 2, a strong
hardy tree, spec. a terebinth, Pistacia
Terebinthus Linn. a tree common in
Palestine, long-lived, and therefore often
employed for landmarks and in designa-
ting places, Gen. 35, 4. Judg. 6, 11. 19.
According to Pliny (16. 12) it is an ever-
green; but this is contrary to the fact.
The ancient versions render it sometimes
a terebinth, and sometimes an oak ; see
more in Thesaur. p. 50, 51. Hence the
word would seem to have been taken in
a broader signification, for any large and
durable tree, like Gr. δρῦς. The modern
name is بُطْم butm ; see Bibl. Res. in
Palest. III. p. 15.
אֱלָהּ Chald. m. emphat. אֱלָהָא, i. q.
Heb. אֱלוֹהַּ a god, generally Dan. 3, 28.
6, 8. 13 ; stat. emphat. spec. of Jehovah
Dan. 2, 20. 3, 32. With a prefix, לֵאלָהּ
2, 19 ; but also with suffix contr. בֵּאלָהֵהּ
Dan. 6, 24. Plur. אֱלָהִין gods Dan. 2, 11.
5, 4. 11. 23. בַּר אֱלָהִין a son of the gods
אֵלֶּה pron. demonstr. plur. comm. these,
Lat. hi, hæ, hæc, employed in common
usage as the plural of זֶה this. The
simple form is אֵל q. v. which is less
frequent; the ending הֶ has a de-
monstrative power, comp. הִנֵּה. Arab.
أُولَى, أُلَى, إِلَا, fem. أُلَاتِ, Ethiop. እሉ
hi, እላ hæ, Chald. אִלֵּין.—It refers both
to what follows, Gen. 2, 4. 6, 9. 11, 10;
and also to what precedes, Gen. 9, 19.
10, 20. 29. 31. Usually put after the
